title: Home, paperwork and officialdom
focus: bhara, bariwala, agrim, chukti, kagojpotro, abedon, sakkhor, soi kora, porichoy potro, meyad, nobikoron, line dewa, sorkari daftor, ghush, dalal
body:
# Home, paperwork and officialdom

Renting a flat or dealing with a government office in Kolkata needs its own vocabulary. Much of the formal Bengali appears on forms and notices, while people at the counter mix in English: advance, agreement, renew, ID proof. Learn both so you can read the notice and talk to the clerk.

| Romanization | Bengali | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| bhara | ভাড়া | rent (the monthly payment) |
| bariwala | বাড়িওয়ালা | landlord / house owner |
| bharate | ভাড়াটে | tenant |
| agrim | অগ্রিম | advance (payment made upfront) |
| chukti | চুক্তি | contract / agreement (formal) |
| kagojpotro | কাগজপত্র | documents / paperwork (collectively) |
| abedon | আবেদন | application (formal request) |
| sakkhor | স্বাক্ষর | signature (formal) |
| soi kora | সই করা | to sign (everyday word) |
| porichoy potro | পরিচয়পত্র | identity card / ID proof |
| meyad | মেয়াদ | validity period / term (of a document, lease) |
| nobikoron | নবীকরণ | renewal (formal) |
| line dewa | লাইন দেওয়া | to stand in line / queue up |
| sorkari daftor | সরকারি দপ্তর | government office |
| ghush | ঘুষ | bribe |
| proman | প্রমাণ | proof (documentary) |
| jorimana | জরিমানা | fine / penalty (money) |
| onumoti | অনুমতি | permission (official) |
| kerani | কেরানি | clerk (office) |
| hoyrani | হয়রানি | harassment / runaround (by officialdom) |
| jachai kora | যাচাই করা | to verify / check (genuineness) |
| bari bodlano | বাড়ি বদলানো | to move house |
| khali kora | খালি করা | to vacate (a flat, room) |
| shesh tarikh | শেষ তারিখ | last date (for submission) |
| joma dewa | জমা দেওয়া | to submit / deposit (form, fee) |
| dalal | দালাল | middleman / tout (at offices) |
| rasid | রসিদ | receipt |

## Which word?

- **sakkhor vs soi**: sakkhor is written and official; soi kora is what you say ("ekhane soi korun").
- **agrim vs advance**: agrim is on paper; at the bariwala's door it's "advance koto?".
- **chukti vs agreement**: for a rental it's the rent agreement. chukti is used for bigger, legal or news contexts.
- **meyad vs nobikoron**: meyad is how long something is valid; nobikoron is renewing it once the meyad ends. In speech: "meyad shesh, renew korte hobe".
- **line dewa**: Kolkata says line dewa for queueing; "queue" is rarely heard.
- **ghush vs dalal**: ghush is the bribe itself; a dalal is the fixer who stands between you and the office.

## Examples

- tin mash-er bhara agrim dite hobe: you'll have to pay three months' rent in advance
- bariwala bolchhe porer mash theke bhara barabe: the landlord says he'll raise the rent from next month
- ekhane ar ekhane soi kore din: please sign here and here
- tomar passport-er meyad shesh hoye jachchhe: your passport is about to expire
- bhor-bela theke line diyechhi: I've been in line since dawn
- ghush na dile file nore na: without a bribe the file doesn't move
- thikana-r proman hishebe electric bill dite paro: you can give an electricity bill as address proof
- ekta certificate-er jonno ki hoyrani: what a runaround for one certificate
- mash-er shesh-e flat khali korte hobe: we have to vacate the flat at the end of the month
- bhara dewar por rasid niye nio: get a receipt after paying the rent

cards.Example: ei flat-er bhara mash-e kuri hajar: the rent on this flat is twenty thousand a month
cards.Notes: bhara dewa = to pay rent; bhara newa = to rent (a place). Also means fare (taxi bhara).

cards.Example: bariwala bolchhe porer mash theke bhara barabe: the landlord says he'll raise the rent from next month
cards.Notes: Landlady: bariwali. Kolkata also says 'owner' for a flat owner.

cards.Example: nichher tola-y notun bharate eshechhe: new tenants have moved in downstairs
cards.Notes: bharatia is a variant; bharate is the usual Kolkata form.

cards.Example: tin mash-er bhara agrim dite hobe: you'll have to pay three months' rent in advance
cards.Notes: In speech everyone says 'advance'; agrim appears in agreements and notices.

cards.Example: sob kagojpotro ekta file-e guchhiye rakho: keep all the paperwork together in one file
cards.Notes: kagoj alone = paper; kagojpotro = the documents. 'documents' is common in offices.

cards.Example: passport-er jonno abedon korechho?: have you applied for the passport?
cards.Notes: abedon kora = to apply. Spoken: 'apply korechho?'. abedonpotro = application form.

cards.Example: protiti pata-y sakkhor lagbe: every page needs a signature
cards.Notes: Formal and written; in speech people say soi.

cards.Example: ekhane ar ekhane soi kore din: please sign here and here
cards.Notes: The spoken word. 'sign kora' is also heard.

cards.Example: dhukte gele porichoy potro dekhate hobe: you need to show ID to get in
cards.Notes: In practice people say 'ID' or name the card (Aadhaar, voter card).

cards.English: validity period / term (of a document, lease)
cards.Example: tomar passport-er meyad shesh hoye jachchhe: your passport is about to expire
cards.Notes: meyad furono = to expire; meyadi = fixed-term (meyadi amanot = fixed deposit).

cards.Example: trade licence-er nobikoron proti bochhor korte hoy: the trade licence has to be renewed every year
cards.Notes: Official word; people mostly say 'renew kora'.

cards.English: to stand in line / queue up
cards.Example: bhor-bela theke line diyechhi: I've been in line since dawn
cards.Notes: The usual Kolkata phrase; line-e darano (stand in line) also works. 'queue' is rarely heard.

cards.Example: sorkari daftor-e kaj korate gele dhoirjo lage: getting anything done at a government office takes patience
cards.Notes: Formal; in speech 'sorkari office'. daftor alone is old-fashioned for office.

cards.Example: deri kore joma dile jorimana dite hobe: if you submit late you'll have to pay a fine
cards.Notes: jorimana kora = to fine someone. 'fine' is also used.

cards.Example: kerani bollen kal asun: the clerk said come tomorrow
cards.Notes: Slightly old-fashioned but very Kolkata; also used dismissively for a desk job.

cards.Example: ekta certificate-er jonno ki hoyrani: what a runaround for one certificate
cards.Notes: hoyran hoye jawa = to be harried and exhausted.

cards.Example: flat kenar age kagojpotro bhalo kore jachai kore nao: verify the papers properly before buying a flat
cards.Notes: Also used for checking a claim or person (verification = jachai).

cards.Example: amra porer mash-e bari bodlachchhi: we're moving house next month
cards.Notes: 'shift kora' is very common in Kolkata (notun flat-e shift korchhi).

cards.Example: mash-er shesh-e flat khali korte hobe: we have to vacate the flat at the end of the month
cards.Notes: khali = empty; also 'chhere dewa' (to give up a place).

cards.Example: form joma dewar shesh tarikh kobe?: when is the last date to submit the form?
cards.Notes: Indian English 'last date' is also used as a loan.

cards.Example: dalal-er kachhe gele kaj taratari hoy, kintu taka beshi lage: a tout gets it done fast, but costs more
cards.Notes: Also a property broker; 'broker' is the neutral loan.

cards.Example: bhara dewar por rasid niye nio: get a receipt after paying the rent
cards.Notes: Spoken: roshid; 'receipt' is also common.

cards.English: What documents do I need to bring?
cards.Romanization: kon kon kagojpotro niye aste hobe?
cards.Bengali: কোন কোন কাগজপত্র নিয়ে আসতে হবে?
cards.Notes: kon kon = which ones (plural). At an office counter you'd say this as is.

cards.English: Who do I need to talk to about this?
cards.Romanization: eta-r byapare kar songe kotha bolte hobe?
cards.Bengali: এটার ব্যাপারে কার সঙ্গে কথা বলতে হবে?
cards.Notes: byapare = regarding; kar songe = with whom (Kolkata prefers songe over sathe).
